## Tayrona Park and the Lost City: what to see in Santa Marta

Romantic Santa Marta, one of Colombia's oldest cities, lies on the Caribbean shore in northern South America, framed by beautiful beaches and the remarkable Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta mountain range. Santa Marta is a major port visited by huge cruise ships, private yachts and cargo vessels. It also attracts Colombians in search of life's simple pleasures: rum, fun and sunshine. At weekends, vacationers fill the beaches or gather along the rocky piers to admire glittering sunsets. The climate is hot, but the heat is drier than in Cartagena, while an evening sea breeze cools the city and makes it pleasant to stroll.

Hidden in the lush mangrove forests of Tayrona National Park are ancient ruins: Ciudad Perdida, the Lost City, described as an ideal destination for a day hike. The ruins of this Tayrona culture settlement, founded around AD 800, were found in 1972 by local tomb raiders.

## Outdoor activities in Santa Marta

You can snorkel or dive along colorful reefs, then stop at a café serving a wide variety of dishes that combine flavors from Latin America, the Caribbean and Europe. As the sun sets, nightlife picks up in the bars and nightclubs around Parque de los Novios.

The twin towers of Santa Prisca rise above the white houses and red roofs of Taxco. The church stands in the historic center, where steep streets converge on a square and workshops specializing in silver.

The church was built in the 18th century at the request of José de la Borda, whose wealth came from silver mining. Its elaborately carved facade and interior decoration show the richness of the Baroque art of that era. Santa Prisca remains an active place of worship, so pilgrimage visits and Mass naturally complement a tour of the town.

Santa Rosa de Cabal is closely linked to coffee farms in the Colombian Andes. On the plantations, visitors learn about coffee cultivation, hand-picking and bean processing. The story continues in a rural kitchen where roasting is demonstrated, while viewpoints overlook the surrounding fields and hillsides.

Thermal waters are another attraction of the region. The Termales de Santa Rosa de Cabal complex welcomes visitors looking to unwind after exploring the coffee-growing area. These experiences reveal two sides of the same destination: rural production and warm natural springs in a mountain setting.

Santa Susana is an Argentine estancia near Los Cardales, in Campana District of Buenos Aires Province. Farming and tourism share the property: visitors come to spend a day in the countryside and discover gaucho traditions.

The ranch experience unfolds amid rural landscapes. The excursion program includes folk entertainment and an Argentine barbecue, an opportunity to enjoy a leisurely lunch and experience daily life on an estancia.

The name Santa Susana is connected with the Kelly family's history. The landowner, Francisco Kelly, named the estate after his wife, Susana Caffrey. Today, the ranch welcomes tourists from Argentina and abroad. It fits easily into a stay in Buenos Aires, with a full day set aside for the countryside program.
